payload.rationale: I estimate a 20% chance that the contract-defined CDC count exceeds 6,000. The supplied CDC summary reports 3,471 confirmed U.S. cases through September 17, including international visitors. YES requires at least 6,001 cases, or 2,530 additional cases. Over roughly 15 remaining weeks, that requires about 169 cases per week—approximately 1.8 times the year-to-date average. Simply extending the average pace would yield about 4,900 cases, below the threshold; this is a benchmark, not a transmission forecast. The reported 39 new outbreaks and 95% outbreak-associated share support allowing substantial upside uncertainty because measles incidence can be concentrated in large, rapidly expanding outbreaks. However, those cumulative statistics do not establish that transmission is currently accelerating. My estimate could be too high if most cases came from earlier outbreaks that are now controlled, leaving little late-year transmission. It could be too low if substantial outbreaks are already accelerating in undervaccinated communities, with school contacts and reporting backlogs producing a sharp increase. I assess the count available under the expiration rules, not a subsequently revised final total; delayed reporting near year-end can therefore prevent otherwise qualifying cases from contributing to settlement.
limitations: No recent weekly case series, outbreak trajectories, or geographic susceptibility data are supplied.
The probability is a judgmental estimate, not the output of a fitted transmission or statistical model.
CDC counts are provisional and subject to reporting delays, revisions, and epidemiological-week assignment; post-expiration revisions do not count.
The supplied full-page capture is truncated before the numerical case total, so the numerical assessment relies on the supplied CDC summary.
